accepted.s: The National Food Security Mission was renamed as which of the following in Financial Year 2024-25?
o: National Food Security and Nutrition Mission
accepted.x: NFSM was renamed the National Food Security and Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) in FY 2024-25.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original mission name from its later official renaming.
accepted.sec: National Missions - focus and crops covered (NFSM, NMSA/RAD, MIDH, NMEO, RKVY)

accepted.s:
With reference to the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA), consider the following statements:
1. It is one of the eight missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change.
2. It focuses on climate-resilient and rainfed farming.
3. It became a sub-mission of Krishonnati from 2018-19.
4. It has been brought under PM-RKVY from 2022-23.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the institutional position and focus of NMSA.
accepted.tq: Track the mission through its parent climate programme, later sub-mission status and recent umbrella scheme.
accepted.sec: National Missions - focus and crops covered (NFSM, NMSA/RAD, MIDH, NMEO, RKVY)

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a component of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture?
accepted.x: RAD, Soil Health Management and Per Drop More Crop are NMSA components. National Agricultural Market is not listed as an NMSA component.
accepted.tq: Find the one item belonging to agricultural marketing rather than the mission’s sustainability components.
accepted.sec: National Missions - focus and crops covered (NFSM, NMSA/RAD, MIDH, NMEO, RKVY)

accepted.s: Under Rainfed Area Development (RAD), assistance of ₹30,000 per family is provided for which of the following?
accepted.x: RAD provides ₹30,000 per family for Integrated Farming System models developed with ICAR support.
accepted.tq: Link the numerical assistance with the specific intervention rather than with a general farm subsidy.
accepted.sec: National Missions - focus and crops covered (NFSM, NMSA/RAD, MIDH, NMEO, RKVY)

accepted.s: Under NMSA, the maximum subsidy mentioned for micro-irrigation is up to:
accepted.x: The micro-irrigation subsidy under NMSA may be provided up to 55%.
accepted.tq: Use the exact percentage and reject nearby rounded subsidy figures.
accepted.sec: National Missions - focus and crops covered (NFSM, NMSA/RAD, MIDH, NMEO, RKVY)

accepted.s: Soil Health Cards under the NMSA-related provision are to be provided free of cost at what interval?
accepted.x: Soil Health Cards are to be provided free every two years, not annually.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the stated biennial interval and the tempting annual alternative.
accepted.sec: National Missions - focus and crops covered (NFSM, NMSA/RAD, MIDH, NMEO, RKVY)

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. NMSA — Agroforestry
2. RAD — ICAR Integrated Farming System models
3. NFSM — Oil palm as its exclusive crop
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Agroforestry is an NMSA component and RAD uses ICAR Integrated Farming System models. NFSM is not exclusively an oil-palm mission.
accepted.tq: Test the mission-component relationship while identifying the overbroad word 'exclusive'.
accepted.sec: National Missions - focus and crops covered (NFSM, NMSA/RAD, MIDH, NMEO, RKVY)

accepted.s:
The Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) covers which of the following?
1. Fruits, vegetables and spices
2. Flowers and mushrooms
3. Coconut, cashew, cocoa and bamboo
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: MIDH covers all the listed horticultural crops and products, including fruits, vegetables, spices, flowers, mushrooms, coconut, cashew, cocoa and bamboo.
accepted.tq: Group the complete crop coverage of a horticulture mission before selecting the code.
accepted.sec: National Missions - focus and crops covered (NFSM, NMSA/RAD, MIDH, NMEO, RKVY)

accepted.s: Which of the following funding ratios is associated with the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture, including its special-region pattern?
o: 60:40 generally and 90:10 for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States
50:50 generally and 75:25 for the North-Eastern States
90:10 generally and 60:40 for the Himalayan States
accepted.x: MIDH follows a 60:40 sharing ratio generally and 90:10 for the North-Eastern and Himalayan regions.
accepted.tq: Compare the normal cost-sharing ratio with the special-region ratio.
accepted.sec: National Missions - focus and crops covered (NFSM, NMSA/RAD, MIDH, NMEO, RKVY)

accepted.s: The National Mission on Edible Oils—Oil Palm was launched in August 2021 with a financial outlay of:
accepted.x: NMEO-Oil Palm was launched in August 2021 with an outlay of ₹11,040 crore and focuses particularly on the North-East and Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
accepted.tq: Separate the oil-palm mission’s outlay from the later oilseeds mission’s outlay.
accepted.sec: National Missions - focus and crops covered (NFSM, NMSA/RAD, MIDH, NMEO, RKVY)

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the National Mission on Edible Oils—Oilseeds announced on 3 October 2024?
o: It focuses on oilseeds, has an outlay of ₹10,103 crore and targets 69.7 MT by 2030-31.
It focuses on horticulture and follows the MIDH funding ratio.
It focuses on pulses and targets 100 MT by 2029-30.
It focuses on oil palm and has an outlay of ₹11,040 crore.
accepted.x: NMEO-Oilseeds was announced on 3 October 2024 with ₹10,103 crore and aims to raise oilseed production from 39 MT to 69.7 MT by 2030-31.
accepted.tq: Separate similar mission names by launch date, crop group, financial outlay and production target.
accepted.sec: National Missions - focus and crops covered (NFSM, NMSA/RAD, MIDH, NMEO, RKVY)

accepted.s: The National Mission on Edible Oils—Oilseeds seeks to increase production from 39 million tonnes to approximately how much by 2030-31?
accepted.x: The target is to raise oilseed production from 39 MT to 69.7 MT by 2030-31.
accepted.tq: Use the stated baseline and target figures rather than calculating an unstated growth rate.
accepted.sec: National Missions - focus and crops covered (NFSM, NMSA/RAD, MIDH, NMEO, RKVY)

accepted.s: Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) primarily aims to:
o: Provide grants to increase State expenditure on agriculture through State-led agricultural plans
Provide only crop insurance to farmers
Replace all State agricultural plans with a centrally fixed crop plan
Finance only oil-palm plantations in the North-Eastern States
accepted.x: RKVY supports State-led agricultural plans by providing grants intended to raise State spending on agriculture. It now functions under the umbrella PM-RKVY framework.
accepted.tq: Identify the scheme’s decentralised State-plan design instead of confusing it with a crop-specific mission.
accepted.sec: National Missions - focus and crops covered (NFSM, NMSA/RAD, MIDH, NMEO, RKVY)

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Technology Mission on Oilseeds, Pulses and Maize
B. National Food Security Mission
C. National Mission on Edible Oils—Oil Palm
D. National Mission on Edible Oils—Oilseeds
accepted.x: The sequence is 1986, 2007, August 2021 and 3 October 2024 respectively.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest 1986 mission and the latest 2024 mission.
accepted.sec: National Missions - focus and crops covered (NFSM, NMSA/RAD, MIDH, NMEO, RKVY)

accepted.s: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana announced for 2025-26 is proposed as a Central Sector scheme covering:
o: All agricultural districts for five years
100 low-performing agricultural districts for six years
accepted.x: The scheme is proposed as a Central Sector scheme for 100 low-performing agricultural districts for six years.
accepted.tq: Match the scheme with its coverage, duration and performance-based district selection.
accepted.sec: National Missions - focus and crops covered (NFSM, NMSA/RAD, MIDH, NMEO, RKVY)

accepted.s: Under the pulses mission associated with the 2025-26 agricultural initiatives, 100% procurement at MSP is proposed for which crops through NAFED and NCCF?
accepted.x: The proposed mission provides 100% MSP procurement of tur, urad and masoor for four years through NAFED and NCCF.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the specified pulse trio from other pulses and oilseeds.
accepted.sec: National Missions - focus and crops covered (NFSM, NMSA/RAD, MIDH, NMEO, RKVY)

accepted.s: After 1991, agriculture’s share in India’s GDP declined from approximately 29.02% to 17.9% by 2014. Which broader development accompanied this change?
o: Complete withdrawal of agriculture from international trade
accepted.x: The decline in agriculture’s GDP share was accompanied by rising rural indebtedness.
accepted.tq: Read the paired trend carefully: falling GDP share was associated with rising, not falling, rural indebtedness.
accepted.sec: Agricultural policy since 1991 - liberalisation and WTO impacts

accepted.s: Which one of the following was an effect of liberalisation after 1991 on Indian agriculture?
o: Replacement of agricultural subsidies by foreign aid
Increase in government investment in agriculture in every period
A ban on all private participation in agriculture
Decline in government investment in agriculture
accepted.x: The stated policy impact of post-1991 liberalisation was a decline in government investment in agriculture.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise policy consequence instead of accepting the positive-sounding reversal.
accepted.sec: Agricultural policy since 1991 - liberalisation and WTO impacts

accepted.s: India’s entry into the WTO in 1995 was associated with which combination in the agricultural sector?
o: Reduced import competition and increased subsidies as a share of farm income
Increased import competition and declining subsidies as a share of farm income
Abolition of all domestic agricultural support
Reduced international trade and unchanged farm incomes
accepted.x: WTO entry increased import competition, while subsidies declined as a share of farm income.
accepted.tq: Pair the two stated effects and reject options that exaggerate them into total abolition or withdrawal.
accepted.sec: Agricultural policy since 1991 - liberalisation and WTO impacts

accepted.s: Who among the following supported globalisation in the debate over agricultural liberalisation?
accepted.x: Sharad Joshi supported globalisation, whereas Tikait of BKU and Nanjundaswamy of KRRS opposed the Dunkel Draft.
accepted.tq: Separate the supporter of globalisation from the organisations and leaders associated with opposition to the Dunkel Draft.
accepted.sec: Agricultural policy since 1991 - liberalisation and WTO impacts

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding WTO boxes:
1. Green Box measures include research, disease control, infrastructure and food security support.
2. Blue Box payments are tied to limiting production.
3. Amber Box includes MSP and input subsidies such as power, fertiliser, seed and irrigation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly identify the measures associated with the Green, Blue and Amber Boxes.
accepted.tq: Match each box with its policy character before choosing the combined code.
accepted.sec: Agricultural policy since 1991 - liberalisation and WTO impacts

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the WTO treatment of the Amber Box?
o: It consists only of decoupled income support.
It is not trade-distorting and is freely allowed without limits.
It carries reduction commitments, subject to de minimis limits of 5% for developed and 10% for developing countries.
It consists of payments tied to limiting production and has no reduction commitment.
accepted.x: Amber Box support is subject to reduction commitments, with de minimis limits of 5% for developed and 10% for developing countries.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Amber Box reduction commitments from Green Box permission and Blue Box production-limitation payments.
accepted.sec: Agricultural policy since 1991 - liberalisation and WTO impacts

accepted.s: The National Agriculture Policy, 2000 was announced in:
accepted.x: The National Agriculture Policy was announced in July 2000.
accepted.tq: Use the announcement date rather than confusing it with the NFSM or NMEO launch dates.
accepted.sec: National Agriculture Policy 2000 - growth target, key thrusts

accepted.s: The National Agriculture Policy, 2000 envisaged annual agricultural growth of:
accepted.x: The policy targeted agricultural growth in excess of 4% per annum.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact threshold and distinguish 'in excess of' from an exact growth rate.
accepted.sec: National Agriculture Policy 2000 - growth target, key thrusts

accepted.s:
Which of the following were key thrusts of the National Agriculture Policy, 2000?
1. Private participation through contract farming and land leasing
2. Price protection and national agricultural insurance
3. A Rainbow Revolution covering all farm sub-sectors
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: The policy emphasised private participation, price protection, agricultural insurance and a broad-based Rainbow Revolution across farm sub-sectors.
accepted.tq: Test the complete set of policy thrusts rather than isolating contract farming alone.
accepted.sec: National Agriculture Policy 2000 - growth target, key thrusts

accepted.s: Which one of the following colour-crop pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Silver Revolution is associated with eggs. Fertilisers are associated with the Grey Revolution.
accepted.tq: Use the colour association and identify the swapped pair between Silver and Grey Revolutions.
accepted.sec: National Agriculture Policy 2000 - growth target, key thrusts

accepted.s: Sustainable agriculture is best understood as the use of land in a manner that:
o: Excludes all modern inputs from farming
Maximises present output regardless of future soil quality
Maintains land quality while meeting present needs without compromising future generations
Uses land only for export-oriented crops
accepted.x: Sustainable agriculture maintains the quality of land while meeting present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs.
accepted.tq: Apply the intergenerational and resource-conservation test to the definition.
accepted.sec: Sustainable agriculture and rainfed areas - meaning, goals, NRAA

accepted.s:
The ultimate goal of sustainable agriculture includes which of the following pillars?
1. Environmental health
2. Economic profitability
3. Social and economic equity
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Sustainable agriculture seeks to combine environmental health, economic profitability and social and economic equity.
accepted.tq: Recognise that sustainability is a three-pillar framework, not merely an environmental objective.
accepted.sec: Sustainable agriculture and rainfed areas - meaning, goals, NRAA

accepted.s: Which statement best distinguishes sustainable agriculture from organic farming?
o: There is no conceptual distinction between the two.
Sustainable agriculture may use synthetic inputs judiciously through approaches such as IPM, precision farming and conservation tillage.
Sustainable agriculture necessarily prohibits all synthetic inputs.
Organic farming permits unlimited synthetic inputs, whereas sustainable agriculture prohibits them.
accepted.x: Unlike a strict organic approach, sustainable agriculture may use synthetic inputs judiciously along with integrated pest management, precision farming and conservation tillage.
accepted.tq: Focus on the qualifying word 'judiciously' when distinguishing the two approaches.
accepted.sec: Sustainable agriculture and rainfed areas - meaning, goals, NRAA

accepted.s: Rainfed farming accounts for approximately what share of India’s net sown area and food production, respectively?
accepted.x: Rainfed farming covers about 50–60% of net sown area and contributes approximately 40% of food production.
accepted.tq: Keep the area share and production share separate; they are not the same percentage.
accepted.sec: Sustainable agriculture and rainfed areas - meaning, goals, NRAA

accepted.s: The National Rainfed Area Authority (NRAA), set up in 2006, is primarily an expert body for:
o: Providing knowledge inputs and coordinating dryland and rainfed upgradation through a watershed approach
Administering MSP procurement in all States
accepted.x: NRAA provides expert knowledge and coordinates the upgrading of dryland and rainfed areas through a watershed approach.
accepted.tq: Match the authority with its dryland, rainfed and watershed functions.
accepted.sec: Sustainable agriculture and rainfed areas - meaning, goals, NRAA

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the pre-Green Revolution phase of agricultural development in India?
o: 1968–81; HYV seeds, fertiliser and irrigation under the New Agricultural Strategy
1987–92; spread of the Green Revolution to rice and other regions
1951–68; exclusive dependence on oilseeds and horticulture
1951–68; land reforms, irrigation, Community Development, PL-480 imports and droughts of 1965–67
accepted.x: The pre-Green Revolution phase covered 1951–68 and included land reforms, irrigation, Community Development, PL-480 imports and the droughts of 1965–67.
accepted.tq: Match the period with its defining features rather than with the later HYV phase.
accepted.sec: Phases of agricultural development in India

accepted.s: The Early Green Revolution phase in India is associated with:
o: 1987–92 and the spread of horticulture alone
1968–81, HYV seeds beginning with wheat, fertiliser, irrigation and the New Agricultural Strategy
accepted.x: The Early Green Revolution phase was 1968–81 and was marked by HYV seeds, initially in wheat, along with fertiliser, irrigation and the New Agricultural Strategy.
accepted.tq: Use the wheat-first HYV clue to identify the Early Green Revolution period.
accepted.sec: Phases of agricultural development in India

accepted.s: The Later Green Revolution phase, covering 1987–92, was characterised by:
o: The spread of the Green Revolution to rice and other regions
Land reforms and Community Development programmes
accepted.x: The Later Green Revolution phase saw the spread of Green Revolution benefits to rice and other regions during 1987–92.
accepted.tq: Match the later period with geographical and crop-wise expansion.
accepted.sec: Phases of agricultural development in India

accepted.s:
Arrange the following phases of agricultural development in India in chronological order:
A. Later Green Revolution
B. Pre-Green Revolution
C. Early Green Revolution
accepted.x: The phases occurred in the order Pre-Green Revolution (1951–68), Early Green Revolution (1968–81) and Later Green Revolution (1987–92).
accepted.tq: Arrange the phases by their stated periods, using the earliest period as the first anchor.
accepted.sec: Phases of agricultural development in India

accepted.s: India’s foodgrain production fell to approximately what level in 1965-66?
accepted.x: Foodgrain production fell to 72.3 million tonnes in 1965-66.
accepted.tq: Recall the historical low-point figure and distinguish it from the later production records.
accepted.sec: Phases of agricultural development in India

accepted.s: Which statement correctly compares India’s recent foodgrain and horticulture production?
o: Horticulture production was below 300 MT in 2024-25.
Foodgrain production was 357.73 MT in 2024-25, while horticulture production was 362.08 MT and therefore higher.
Foodgrain production was 362.08 MT, while horticulture production was 357.73 MT.
Both foodgrain and horticulture production were exactly 357.73 MT.
accepted.x: Foodgrain production was recorded at 357.73 MT in 2024-25, while horticulture production reached 362.08 MT, making horticulture larger.
accepted.tq: Compare the two close figures carefully and identify which production category is higher.
accepted.sec: Phases of agricultural development in India
